_comment: The HRV decision tree as used by MCC and the Mindbook. 'parent' gives the tree. Sub-nodes of N11 carry their own verdicts and roll up to N11 by the worst (most binding) sub-node tier. 'ruled_out_requires_families' (v0.1.2) lists evidence families (connectors_not_built ids or registry family ids) at least one of which must be present before the node can be ruled_out; until then the node caps at probably_not and the blocker names the missing family.

price.label: Test 1: Price
price.description: If the constraint binds, its price or shadow price is high, or agents are rationed at the going price.

changes.label: Test 2: Changes
changes.description: When the constraint eases or tightens, investment and growth respond.

circumvention.label: Test 3: Circumvention
circumvention.description: Agents pay to get around the constraint: generators, self-finance, informality, emigration.

camels.label: Test 4: Camels and hippos
camels.description: Activities light in the constrained factor survive and thrive; intensive ones do not.

nodes.label: First decision: cost of finance versus low returns
nodes.question: Is private investment low because projects cannot get finance at a reasonable price, or because there are few projects worth financing?
nodes.if_binding: Real lending rates high relative to expectation; firms rationed; investment responds to rates; firms bypass banks.
nodes.if_not: Real rates at or below expectation; banks liquid; firms not seeking credit; investment unresponsive to rates.

nodes.label: Bad international finance
nodes.question: Can the country borrow abroad at a reasonable cost?
nodes.if_binding: Poor ratings and high spreads; sudden stops; growth only when foreign financing is available; heavy external debt.
nodes.if_not: Spreads near expectation; current account comfortably financed; FDI flowing in.

nodes.label: Low domestic savings
nodes.question: Does society save too little, with foreign savings unable to substitute?
nodes.if_binding: High real deposit rates; low savings relative to expectation; growth tied to terms of trade and inflows.
nodes.if_not: Deposit rates at or below expectation; savings at or above expectation; or international finance available.

nodes.label: Poor financial intermediation
nodes.question: Do savings reach investors expensively or not at all?
nodes.if_binding: Wide spreads; high real lending rates; firms fully credit constrained; banks lending to government; self-financing.
nodes.if_not: Spreads and rates near expectation; liquid banks; firms with credit access; no crowding out.

nodes.label: Low human capital
nodes.question: Are skills scarce enough to make projects unprofitable?
nodes.if_binding: High returns to schooling; firms train in-house; firms cite skills; skill-intensive sectors lag.
nodes.if_not: Educated unemployment high; returns to schooling low; firms do not cite skills (the South Africa case).

nodes.label: Bad infrastructure: electricity
nodes.question: Is unreliable or costly power making projects unprofitable?
nodes.if_binding: Large lost sales from outages; long connection delays; generator ownership; high losses.
nodes.if_not: Outage losses and delays near expectation; no self-generation pattern.

nodes.label: Bad infrastructure: transport and logistics
nodes.question: Are transport and logistics costs making trade and production unprofitable?
nodes.if_binding: High trade costs; poor logistics performance; losses in transit; specialization in low weight-to-value goods.
nodes.if_not: Trade costs and logistics performance near expectation.

nodes.label: Bad infrastructure: ICT, water and irrigation
nodes.question: Are connectivity or water constraints binding?
nodes.if_binding: Penetration and prices far from expectation.

nodes.label: Land markets and tenure
nodes.question: Is access to land or tenure security constraining investment?
nodes.if_binding: Firms cite land; registration slow and costly; tenure insecurity high.
nodes.if_not: Low complaint after conditioning; registration near expectation.

nodes.label: Geography, natural capital and market size
nodes.question: Context, not a removable constraint.

nodes.label: Macroeconomic risk
nodes.question: Do inflation, fiscal or exchange-rate risks make returns unappropriable?
nodes.if_binding: High or volatile inflation; parallel premium; debt distress; dollarization; investment responds to stabilization.
nodes.if_not: Prices, exchange rate and fiscal indicators near expectation; no crisis in window.

nodes.label: Microeconomic risks
nodes.question: Do property rights, corruption, taxes, regulation, crime or policy uncertainty make returns unappropriable?

nodes.label: Property rights and expropriation
nodes.question: Are returns at risk of expropriation or unenforceable contracts?

nodes.label: Corruption
nodes.question: Does corruption tax or endanger returns?

nodes.label: Taxes and tax administration
nodes.question: Do tax rates or administration take or endanger returns?

nodes.label: Regulation, competition and barriers to entry
nodes.question: Do regulation or protected incumbents block entry and returns?

nodes.label: Crime and security
nodes.question: Do crime and insecurity tax returns?

nodes.label: Policy and political uncertainty
nodes.question: Do reversals and instability make returns unpredictable?

nodes.label: Self-discovery and information externalities
nodes.question: Is discovering what the country can produce profitably under-rewarded?
nodes.if_binding: Negative complexity gap; few nearby products; low transition frequency; and other constraints not binding.
nodes.if_not: Complexity at or above expectation; healthy new-product entry.

nodes.label: Coordination failures
nodes.question: Are missing sector-specific public inputs blocking activities? Cannot be judged from macro data; sector work required.
